releases.title: Greek letter reader
releases.summary: A small learned reader that proposes Greek capital letters, with boxes and confidences, on ink-detection maps and drawn ink labels, and on photographs of papyri. Reading needs only NumPy, with no GPU or deep-learning framework, and every result carries null and orientation controls and a status code, with a control map when one is given. Its output is a hypothesis for a person to check, not a reading. Its default weights, `letters-v2-ccby`, are released under CC BY 4.0; the earlier `letters-v2-real` (CC BY-NC 4.0) stays available. With `letters-v2-ccby`, on PHerc. 1667's official ink labels it names drawn letters at a character error of 0.043 with the line given, and on PHerc. 1667's ink maps of the same groups its free-ends error is 0.31 to 0.48 (plain character error 0.76 to 1.39, which also charges letters read beside the labelled ones), measured under rules fixed before the reads (Model output; 117 letters in 84 groups, scored against machine transcriptions of the drawings). Those segments are in `ink_9um`'s training labels, and whether the 2.4 um model that made their maps trained on them is not checked, so their maps may be cleaner than maps of new text. On these tests `letters-v2-ccby` has not been shown to read better than `letters-v2-real`, and it errs more on one of the map rows; it is the default for its licence (Interpretation). How well it names letters on real photographs is untested.
releases.details: `scrolls-letterdemo` checks the install on synthetic letters (it downloads the 6 MB of weights once) and prints DEMO PASS. `--letter-px 86` is PHerc. 1667's letter height on the 38 um grid of the public-map demo, `scripts/letters/demo_p1667.py`. Give the reader its own virtual environment, apart from AutoPipeline's: both install a package named `kit`. Windows, other letter sizes, that demo, both model cards and benchmarks: [`docs/letter-reader.md`](docs/letter-reader.md).

releases.title: Scroll centre (umbilicus) finder
releases.summary: Finds the winding centre (the umbilicus) of a Herculaneum scroll in X-ray CT and writes it in the format of the published umbilicus files, one control point per height. It reads every 8th level-3 slice of the scroll's 1.2 m (about 9 um) scan from the open-data bucket with range requests; two small U-Nets place the centre, the first on the slice squeezed to 256 pixels and the second on a 12 to 13 mm window round the first answer, and two end trims drop heights where a centre has nothing to sit on. Scored against the 13 published centre lines with each scroll held out of its own models' training, the median distance over all 3,414 scored slices is 0.73 mm (90th percentile 3.37 mm), against 3.98 mm for the papyrus centroid control; over the 3,243 of those slices that the end trims keep, close to what a written line holds (this score's mount and cap trim used level-5 planes), it is 0.69 mm (Model output, two training runs of 13 October 2026). Each reference is one person's line, two people placing the same centre often disagree by a few millimetres, and the settings were chosen while looking at some of the same scrolls. The line is model output: check it on CT slices before you rely on it.
commands: python -m pip install numpy scipy requests torch
for f in umbilicus-first-all.pt umbilicus-zoom-all.pt; do curl -fL -o work/umbilicus/weights/$f $U/$f; done
python -m unittest tests.test_umbilicus          # synthetic data, CPU
releases.details: Guide, the 14 weight files with their SHA-256, held-out results with their limits, the end-point rule, training and licences: [`scripts/umbilicus/README.md`](scripts/umbilicus/README.md); evidence: [`docs/evidence/2026-10-14-umbilicus/`](docs/evidence/2026-10-14-umbilicus/README.md).

releases.title: AutoPipeline
releases.summary: AutoPipeline runs villa's pipeline from a released scan to a scored ink map, with a rule written down before the run in place of each choice a person usually makes by eye, and a control beside every check. It drives VC3D's command-line tools and villa's ink detection end to end: umbilicus, seed points, tracing with the published normal grids, surface checks, flattening, rendering, ink detection with reversed and shuffled maps, and scoring against published ink labels. Its default reader is now Domenico Russo's Reader v2, a community fine-tune of `ink_9um`: on PHerc0841 w00, from the released scan and the published segment, it scored AUC 0.8752 forward and 0.5659 reversed, against 0.7479 and 0.5012 for `ink_9um` seed 42 on the same render (Model output, development data, 15 October 2026). Traces grown from its own seed points are small patches with no held-out ink score yet. This is version 0.1.4, the fourth fix release: it passes remote volumes to VC3D's renderer in the form villa's builds since 12 October 2026 require (they refuse 0.1.3's), though no full remote render has run with it yet; the earlier releases stay on their own branches. Its last step, ink detection with the reversed-layer control, also runs in a browser with `ink_9um` seed 42: the [AutoPipeline ink Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/autopipeline-ink) maps a crop of a released segment, or a small surface volume you upload, and scores the crop where it has published ink labels.
commands: python -m pip install -e .                      # numpy, tifffile, zarr 3, scipy
python scripts/demo_synthetic.py                # every step on a synthetic scroll; prints DEMO PASS
releases.details: Setup, the run monitor and the limits: the package's [README](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-fix4/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix4/autopipeline/README.md). What changed: [in 0.1.4](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-fix4/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix4/CHANGES.md) and [in 0.1.3](https://github.com/ChaseHendrick/Scrolls/blob/submission/progress-2026-10-fix3/submissions/progress-2026-10-fix3/CHANGES.md).

releases.title: StrokeNet text-likeness score
releases.summary: A small learned score for how much a 6.1 mm window of an organisers' ink map looks like lines of text, with rotation and IAAFT controls reported with every result. It needs only NumPy to run. Its held-out test on six PHerc. Paris 4 tracings, fixed before the read, is published in full: it misses its preregistered bar on two of nine items (blank papyrus against its own 90 degree turn, and blank windows above the threshold), simple scores such as ink density match it on the other items, and it beats every simple score only at telling text from its 90 degree turn (AUC 0.994 against 0.865). A score is model output, not a reading.
commands: python -m kit strokenet MAP.tif --pixel-mm 0.0024 --json          # weights downloaded once, SHA-256 checked
releases.details: Model card, held-out results and the tile grid pilot: [`docs/strokenet.md`](docs/strokenet.md).

releases.title: Segment stack check
releases.summary: Checks a stack of consecutive tifxyz segments of one scroll against the scroll's umbilicus, from segment geometry alone (no CT, no model): order on rays from the umbilicus every degree, adjacent segments that coincide or are spaced unlike the pairs near them, missing sectors of one winding or of several adjacent ones, skipped windings, turn overlaps and the ends of the stack. It reads local folders or the open-data bucket, writes a JSON report, and writes per-vertex masks to drop before a spiral fit or a relative winding count. On PHerc0139 w023 to w040 it measured that w035 covers a median 258 degrees of its turn, leaving a gap (followed from z 9,000 to 27,800, a median 98 degrees wide) where w036 lies a median 17 um outside w034, against 242 um where w035 is present, by an amount that swings with height from 96 um inside to 174 um outside; that near their ends w035 and w036 are missing together; that w035 lies inside w034 on 10 % of the rays that cross both (7 % by more than 18.72 um); and that w023 to w034 are each traced a median 28 to 48 degrees per grid line past a full turn (66 for w026), with more than half of each doubly traced end within 18.72 um of the next segment for w023 to w031 but not for w032 to w034 (measured from the published segments and umbilicus, 14 October 2026). Geometry alone cannot say which segment left its sheet; the note adds a look at the CT at 12 places.
commands: python -m pip install numpy tifffile scipy
python -m unittest tests.test_stackcheck      # synthetic stacks: a clean spiral passes, each planted defect is flagged
releases.details: Usage, the PHerc0139 numbers, example vertices for VC3D, the CT look and limits: [`docs/logs/2026-10-14-pherc0139-segment-defects.md`](docs/logs/2026-10-14-pherc0139-segment-defects.md); each check is described in [`kit/stackcheck.py`](kit/stackcheck.py).

releases.title: Unroll (interactive 3D scroll viewer)
releases.summary: [Unroll](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll) is an interactive 3D viewer that virtually unrolls Herculaneum scroll scans with ink layers, an Ink Bench for comparing ink models, CT tools and an agent API. Status: released. Version: 1.5.0 (the Space's `version.json` and `CHANGELOG.md`). It shows nine scrolls from the Vesuvius Challenge open data, each as its traced segments with an X-ray layer, plus the published ink detection where the open data has it; PHerc. 139 also has an ink_9um (9 µm) layer over all 37 windings. The CT tools (1.2.0 to 1.5.0) add X-ray window and level with auto contrast, a CT volume view that shows a cube of the raw scan around any point of the papyrus, the traced segments drawn into that cube, and streaming from the open data bucket. Licence: Apache 2.0 for all code; the scan data and everything derived from it are CC BY-NC 4.0. It runs in the browser with no install or account, and it can also be installed as an app that works offline. Ink layers show where models detect ink; letters visible here are candidates for expert reading.
releases.details: Opens at [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/unroll). Install app: open [sharpmeow-unroll.static.hf.space](https://sharpmeow-unroll.static.hf.space/) and press Install app in the View panel or Settings (or use the browser's install icon); the page and the default scroll then work offline. Layers, controls and credits: [`docs/unroll-space.md`](docs/unroll-space.md).

releases.title: Scroll Lens (3D DINO, ink and surface models on scan cubes)
releases.summary: [Scroll Lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens) shows what the Vesuvius Challenge's 3D models see inside a scroll scan. Pick one of 99 ready-made cubes or a point in one of twelve public 2.2 to 2.4 µm scans, and it runs the organizers' 3D DINO embeddings (dinovol), direct 3D ink model and recto surface model on a 128³ or 256³ cube read live from the open data. The three slice views are drawn in your browser, so sliders, dragging, zoom and layers answer at once. Click a patch to light up every patch the DINO model finds alike, the organizers' own few-click recipe; the concept carries across scans and downloads as `concept.npy`. Each cube shows how well the organizers' ink reference agrees with the ink model, beside controls that must fail. For scripts and agents, eight API endpoints (also MCP tools) list the scans and the gallery, search cubes, draw slices (all three views in one image) and run the models. Status: released. Version: 1.1.0. It runs on ZeroGPU and falls back to the CPU when a visitor's GPU time runs out. License: Apache 2.0 for the code; the models are MIT; the scan data and the gallery cubes derived from it are CC BY-NC 4.0. Model output, not a reading: a cube is smaller than one letter.
releases.details: Opens at [huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens](https://huggingface.co/spaces/SharpMeow/scroll-lens); MCP at `https://sharpmeow-scroll-lens.hf.space/gradio_api/mcp/`. Source and tests: [`spaces/scroll-lens/`](spaces/scroll-lens/). Guide: [`docs/tools/scroll-lens.md`](docs/tools/scroll-lens.md).
